title: On Assessing the damage field by field
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：assess　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 assess 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the engineer ① assessed the damage field by field without a word of thanks, and every worker in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the engineer ② assesses the damage field by field at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ assess the damage field by field at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ assessed the damage field by field before — a line in the manual for April 1954 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Assessing the damage field by field without a word of thanks, the engineer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ assess the progress of the child at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Assess the progress of the child at once and never mention it again.

By 1967 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the manual, and a new worker from the next workshop ⑧ assesses the progress of the child without a word of thanks every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply  assessed the damage field by field again when nobody else would.

To assess the damage field by field, my mother said in 1972, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody assesses the damage field by field at once again and somebody must assess the damage field by field without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 评估（一般过去式 assessed the damage field by field：1960 年工程师头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 评估（一般现在 assesses the damage field by field：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 评估（不定式 to assess the damage field by field：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 评估（过去完成时 had assessed the damage field by field：1954 年四月的说明书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 评估（动名词 assessing the damage field by field 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 评定（assess the progress of the child：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去评定那个孩子的进步）
G. v. 评定（assess the progress of the child：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 评估（后段两处：新来的工人照例 assesses the progress of the child，而母亲又一次 assessed the damage field by field）

answers.why: assess 意为“评估”，1960 年工程师不图一句谢评估一块田一块田地估那损失，那是车间里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 assessed。
assess 意为“评估”，自那以后工程师二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 assesses。
assess 意为“评估”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯评估一块田一块田地估那损失”，此处为不定式 to assess the damage field by field。
assess 意为“评估”，说明书里 四月 那行字说明早在 1967 年之前就有人评估过，故用过去完成时 had assessed。
assess 意为“评估”，工程师说“评估一块田一块田地估那损失这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 assessing the damage field by field 作主语。
assess 意为“评定”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去评定那个孩子的进步”，should ever 之后用原形 assess the progress of the child。
assess 意为“评定”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻评定那个孩子的进步（assess the progress of the child at once），以后再也不要提起。
assess 意为“评估”，新来的工人每个年头都照例评定那个孩子的进步，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 assesses。

Somebody had assessed the damage field by field long before 1967, and the line in the manual for April proves it.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 assess 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the engineer assessed the damage field by field without a word of thanks, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the engineer assesses the damage field by field at once whenever the workshop asks.
Assessing the damage field by field without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever assess the progress of the child at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next workshop assesses the progress of the child without a word of thanks every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother assessed the damage field by field again, and the workshop remembered that half.
